Who Am I?

I am Senal Dilanjana, a Linux-Native Technologist and IT undergraduate at the University of Vavuniya. I focus on securing digital infrastructures and optimizing system workflows.

My daily driver is Arch Linux, and I spend my time engineering secure, self-hosted automation infrastructures and testing them. I am deeply interested in security auditing, ethical hacking, and agentic AI workflows.

Outside of the terminal, I enjoy exploring Linux customization and staying updated on CI/CD pipelines. I value collaboration and have experience leading development teams in university and independent environments.

Journal

Linux Feb 04, 2026

Decoding the Wire: How I Built a Raw Socket Sniffer in Python

In an era of encrypted traffic and high-level APIs, the actual mechanics of how data moves across a wire can feel like "magic." To demystify this, I built NetSniff—a low-level network monitor that bypasses the standard OS abstractions to see the raw binary heartbeat of a network.
